overall_reason: Instrument Sans at weight 400 is set with care at display size (leading 1.0, -0.025em tracking, 60 to 160px), but it is a saturated face with no stated source, and the page wraps it in the generator's habits: three headings whose second sentence turns grey, an outlined accent word, and 30 JetBrains Mono labels, five of them tracked caps.

score.reason: T-LEADING and T-MEASURE pass with a tuned display setting, but T-TYPE-SOURCE finds a saturated face with no argument, T-HEAD-TREATMENT finds four set-apart heading parts, T-LADDER finds 13 sizes and h3 in five sizes, and T-LABEL-TRANSFORM fails on the mono caps labels.

findings.title: Headings are set in one voice
findings.where: section h2s "Everything you need.", "Three steps.", "Built by devs." and "Simple, transparent pricing", 1440 (tiles/1440-01.png, 1440-03.png, 1440-09.png, 1440-10.png)
findings.evidence: The type table lists three h2s whose second sentence is set apart by colour at 60px: "Nothing you don't.", "Infinite possibilities." and "For devs." turn grey under a black first sentence. The pricing h2 sets "pricing" as outlined, unfilled letters (tiles/1440-10.png top). That is four set-apart heading parts with no single hero signature.
findings.before: "Everything you need. / Nothing you don't." with the second line in grey, repeated in three sections, plus one outlined word
findings.after: Each h2 in one colour and one fill; if the page needs a signature, keep one treatment on one heading
findings.why: The same two-tone formula on every section head turns a display setting into a template, and the reader learns to skip the grey half.

findings.title: Saturated faces need an argument
findings.evidence: fonts.json at 1440 shows Instrument Sans drawing 303 elements in every role (display at 60 to 160px, h3, body, controls, small text) and JetBrains Mono drawing 37 labels. data/lexicons/fonts.yaml lists Instrument Sans as saturated. There is no contract or brand file to supply a reason, and the brand "Optimus" has no wordmark face of its own (tiles/1440-00.png top left).
findings.before: Instrument Sans in every role plus JetBrains Mono labels, with no stated source
findings.after: A display face chosen for the brief (see substitutes in data/lexicons/fonts.yaml), or a recorded reason for Instrument Sans in the contract
findings.why: Instrument Sans over JetBrains Mono is a pairing many generated developer landing pages share, so the type gives this product no voice of its own.

findings.title: Monospace only for code and figures
findings.where: section labels span.font-mono.text-xs, stat sources, pricing numbers, 1440 and 375
findings.evidence: The type table counts 32 small mono elements at 1440 and 49 at 375. They are not code: "The platform for modern teams", "Capabilities", "Process", "Live metrics" (eyebrow labels behind a rule, tiles/1440-01.png and 1440-05.png), "STRIPE" and "NOTION" under the hero stats, and "01", "02", "03" over the pricing tiers. The sweep's numbered_labels hit covers the pricing numbers. Only the workflow.ts sample (tiles/1440-03.png) is code.
findings.before: JetBrains Mono for eyebrows, company names and tier numbers
findings.after: Mono only in the code sample and the live clock; labels in Instrument Sans at the small step
findings.why: Mono on every label is a borrowed developer costume; it adds a third texture without telling the reader anything.

findings.title: Small labels earn their caps
findings.evidence: The type table finds 5 small labels set in uppercase with 0.1em tracking at 12px: "TRUSTED BY FORWARD-THINKING TEAMS", "KEY RESULT", "PRICING", "MOST POPULAR" and "WHAT PEOPLE SAY". With the caps and tracking removed, "Trusted by forward-thinking teams" and "Key result" read as well or better.
findings.after: Sentence case at 14px in the body face, or remove the label where the heading already says it ("Pricing" sits over "Simple, transparent pricing")
findings.why: Tracked caps at 12px slow reading and repeat the heading below them.

findings.title: One size per kind of element
findings.evidence: The type table gives h3 at 30px (6), 36px (4), 18px (4), 16px (4) and 14px (4), and the sweep's type_ladder hit counts 13 distinct sizes on the page (12 to 160px). Feature titles ("Instant Deployment", 36px, tiles/1440-01.png) and step titles ("Connect your tools", 30px, tiles/1440-03.png) do the same job at different sizes. The sweep's flat_hierarchy hit puts some h3s at the 18px body size.
findings.before: h3 in five sizes, 13 sizes on the page
findings.after: One section-item title size (for example 30px) and a ladder of about 8 steps
findings.why: Five h3 sizes make the reader re-learn the hierarchy in every section.

strengths: The display setting is tuned: Instrument Sans at weight 400, leading 1.0 and -0.025em tracking from 60 to 160px.
Measure is short and even: a median of 33 characters a line at 1440 and 29.5 at 375, with no paragraph over 75.
The stylesheet sets tabular-nums, and the live counters ("2,847,392", "99.99%") hold their width.
not_investigated: T-FONT-RENDERED: the sweep's fallback_face hit lists 4 small elements drawn in Consolas or the wrong face; the main faces drew, so face judgments stand.
T-PUNCTUATION: 2 straight double quotes and 3 straight apostrophes, no curly marks; consistent, so no finding under C32, though the 60px testimonial quote ends in a straight mark.
T-HEADLINE-FIT: the hero "The platform to scale" is a div, not an h1; h2s hold to 2 lines at 1440 and 3 at 375.
Eyebrows, widows and 14px text are the sweep's (eyebrow, widows, text_floor).
